statements.t: “The $8.0 million funding commitment I provided to the Company on November 11, 2026 is intended to reinforce the balance sheet while we complete the build-out of the Bridgeport facility and continue to advance the Project LightShift quantum antenna program under our newly expanded field of use.

The Company believes the commitment is intended to supplement its working capital as it continues to build out its autonomous defense manufacturing capacity at the Bridgeport facility and to advance its Quantum Drones programs.

The Company currently expects to begin manufacturing and selling drones in early 2027, subject to further build-out of production lines, procurement of equipment, and completion of commercial prototypes.

On November 6, 2026, the Company’s wholly owned subsidiary, Quantum Drones Corporation, and Project LightShift, Inc. entered into a First Amendment to their June 2026 exclusive worldwide license agreement covering Project LightShift’s patent-protected quantum photonic array, or quantum antenna, technology.
We anticipate investing in research and development to power the ultimate commercialization of our drone technology.

The Company intends to use the Bridgeport facility to expand its focus to developing intelligent, scalable platforms that integrate AI and quantum computing to power next-generation control systems for unmanned vehicles, aerial vehicles and underwater vehicles, such as drones, self-driving cars and robotic fleets.

The Company aims to accelerate the convergence of AI and quantum technologies to deliver safer, more capable, and more efficient autonomous systems for defense, commercial logistics, disaster response, and critical infrastructure operations.

As part of this development strategy, we expect to use the management expertise and some of the personnel and specialty metal fabrication capabilities of Arcade Technology, which is housed in the Bridgeport facility being built out for our drone manufacturing business.
The commencement of drone manufacturing has taken longer than we initially anticipated, primarily due to facility build-out delays.

We currently expect to begin manufacturing and selling drones in early 2027; however, there can be no assurance that we will achieve this timeline or that our drone products will achieve market acceptance.

In the meantime, we continue to operate the precision metal stamping business acquired from Arcade Technology at the Bridgeport facility, which generated all of our revenue from continuing operations for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, and we intend to continue operating this business while we pursue our drone strategy.

In addition, we recorded in-process research and development expense of $4,258,449 related to the license of a quantum antenna from Project LightShift in June 2026, which was expensed because the licensed technology is still in process and has a single field of use.

Pursuant to the Lazar Purchase Agreement, the net proceeds of the Investment will be used for our operations, including for general corporate and working capital purposes, for expenses related to the Investment and to satisfy certain agreed upon obligations.

We plan to fund our cash flow and working capital needs through current cash on hand and future debt and/or equity financings which we may obtain through one or more public or private equity offerings, debt financings, government or other third-party funding, strategic alliances or collaboration agreements.

Management’s plans may also include reducing or deferring certain discretionary expenditures and pursuing strategic partnerships and/or revenue-generating contracts; however, there can be no assurance these plans will be effectively implemented or be successful.
There can be no assurance that the Company will be able to obtain additional financing on terms that are favorable to the Company, or at all.

Shares will be offered under the Company’s shelf registration statement on Form S-3 (File No. 333-296480), which was declared effective by the SEC on June 15, 2026, and a related prospectus supplement dated October 9, 2026.

Based on our cash on hand and the Funding Commitment, management has concluded that our plans alleviate this substantial doubt, and we believe we will have sufficient resources to fund our planned operations and meet our obligations as they become due for at least the next twelve months from the date of this Quarterly Report.

These estimates had a significant effect on our results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, including $3.3 million of acquired in-process research and development expense attributable to ordinary shares issued for the Project LightShift license and $3.2 million of share-based compensation for shares issued or issuable to non-employees for services.
